intro: Send one message to many customers at once, by email, SMS, a chat app or in the app, and see how it did: who opened it, who clicked and the sales that followed. People are only sent what they agreed to, and every campaign can wait for an approver before it goes.
start: Check your campaign categories, so people can choose which kinds of message they get.
Save an audience for the customers you write to most.
Write your first campaign, send yourself a test, then send it for review.

articles.title: Send a campaign to your customers
articles.summary: Write the message, choose who it is for, see who it will reach, then send it now or at a time you choose.

steps.rest: Give it a name, choose the channel and the category it belongs to.
on the Message tab. Add their first name or their way off the list where you want them. Press Send test to see it yourself.
on the Audience tab: one of your saved audiences, or people chosen just for this campaign.
It shows how many will be sent it, who is left out and why, and the message as one person will see it.
With an approval policy, it waits for an approver. With none, the button says Approve and continue, and it is approved at once.
and choose the day and the time. Nothing is sent until it is approved and you choose a time.

articles.after: Once it has gone, Results shows how many were delivered, opened, clicked and replied, and the sales that followed it.
tips: Pause stops anything more from going until you resume it.
Cost shows the campaign's budget beside what the books say it cost.
Duplicate starts a new campaign from one you sent before.

articles.title: Save an audience to send campaigns to
articles.summary: Choose who a campaign goes to by who they are, what they bought and what they owe, and keep it to use again.

articles.title: Set the kinds of message people can choose
articles.summary: Categories say what a message is about. Marketing ones need consent; people choose which they get.

steps.rest: give it a name and say what it covers. It is shown to people choosing what they get.
Marketing, which needs their consent, or Informational, which goes to everyone who has not turned it off.
